gaps.sentence: We arrived at the hotel at noon, ___ the rooms were not ready.
gaps.explanation: 'When' introduces non-defining clauses about time after a comma; 'that' is impossible after a comma.

gaps.sentence: The people ___ live upstairs are very quiet.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' is the subject relative for people.

gaps.sentence: Nobody knows the reason ___ he resigned so suddenly.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why ...' is the standard pattern; 'why' means 'for which'.

gaps.sentence: That's exactly ___ I needed — thank you!
gaps.explanation: 'What I needed' means 'the thing that I needed'; 'that' cannot be used in this free relative position.

gaps.sentence: Have you got anything ___ will remove this stain?
gaps.explanation: After 'anything', 'that' is the preferred relative pronoun; 'which' is avoided after -thing words.

gaps.sentence: 1998 was the year ___ the factory finally closed.
The restaurant ___ we had dinner last night has excellent reviews.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' replaces 'in which' after place nouns; no preposition appears in the clause.

gaps.sentence: The girl ___ sits behind me in class is from Peru.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to a person who is the subject; 'which' refers only to things.
